title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is studying the 'Teichmüller tower' in profinite form. N_{1,1}^~ is the extended mapping-class/automorphism group attached to M_{1,1}. It sits in an exact sequence 1 → SL(2,Z)^ → N_{1,1}^~ → Γ_Q^~ → 1 (previous page, (5)). Here SL(2,Z)^ = π1^(M_{1,1}) is the profinite completion of the genus-1 mapping class group. Γ_Q^~ = Γ_{0,3}^~ is a GT-type group: the group of automorphisms of the genus-0 three-point level, which receives Gal(Q̄/Q).

(9) The extension splits: N_{1,1}^~ ≃ N_{1,1}^~(0) · SL(2,Z)^ (semi-direct), with N_{1,1}^~(0) ≃ M_{0,3}^~(0) ≃ Γ_Q^~. This is a section, presumably coming from a tangential base point at the cusp/degeneration. Hence Γ_Q^~ acts genuinely, not just by outer automorphisms, on SL(2,Z)^, and he wants this action explicitly.

Tool (10): the cartesian square SL(2,Z)^ = SL(2,Ẑ) ×_{SL(2,Ẑ)/±1} (SL(2,Z)^/±1). Here SL(2,Z)^/±1 = PSL(2,Z)^ ≃ G_{0,3}^{+^}, the profinite oriented cartographic group (Z/2 * Z/3)^ generated by σ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). The right vertical arrow is induced by (2).

Action on the cartographic group: an element v of Γ_Q^~ is encoded by a pair (α,β) in Π̂_{0,3} (α in a suitable coset/subset) satisfying the 'équation des lacets' (12): αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1} ℓ_1^ν, with ν ∈ Ẑ. Here ρ and σ act as automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} = π1^(P^1−{0,1,∞}) permuting the three points. This is Grothendieck's path-theoretic version of the GT (Drinfeld/Ihara) relations: α and β are paths between tangential base points. v acts on G_{0,3}^{+^} by (13): ρ ↦ int(α)ρ = ξρ with ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, and σ ↦ int(β)σ = ησ with η = βσ(β)^{-1}.

Compatibility: this action is compatible, through PSL(2,Ẑ), with conjugation on SL(2,Ẑ) by the image u̲ of u under (8). The next page makes this precise: u̲ = diag(μ,1) with μ = χ(u) the cyclotomic character. Combining both, the next page obtains the action on SL(2,Z)^ itself: ρ ↦ int(α̃)ρ and σ ↦ ε·int(β̃)σ, with ε = ε_2(μ) = ±1 according as μ ≡ ±1 mod 4. So the GT/Galois action on profinite SL(2,Z) is the lift of the cartographic action, corrected by a sign on the order-4 generator governed by χ mod 4.

Purpose: explicit description of the Galois/GT action on π1^(M_{1,1}) = SL(2,Z)^, i.e. the genus-1 level of the Teichmüller tower in terms of genus-0 data.
errors: Top-left of (10) should read SL(2,Z)^ (profinite completion of SL(2,Z)), not SL(2,Ẑ)^; with that reading the square is indeed cartesian. The reason: ±1 injects into SL(2,Z)^ (it is detected in SL(2,Z/3)) and is the kernel of SL(2,Z)^ → PSL(2,Z)^.
In 'qui opère sur G_{0,3}^{+^} ≃ Sl(2,Z)^/' the '±1' is omitted.

The precise domain of α in (11) is unclear: some coset/subset of Π̂_{0,3} written with an underbrace and a correction involving ℓ_0, ℓ_∞ (or τ_∞). The conditions on (α,β) needed to define an element of Γ_Q^~ are not fully stated on this page.
No genuine mathematical error is visible. The formula u(ρ) = int(α)ρ = ξρ is consistent if ρ, σ are read as automorphisms and ρ(α) as the transformed path.

ideas.what: Splitting of the extension 1→SL(2,Z)^→N_{1,1}^~→Γ_Q^~→1 via N_{1,1}^~(0) ≃ Γ_Q^~, giving an honest action of Γ_Q^~ on SL(2,Z)^
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on π1 of M_{1,1} with tangential base point at the cusp
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Teichmüller tower and genus-1 level; La Longue Marche (circulated 1981) discusses Γ_Q action on the tower

ideas.modern_name: fibre product description of profinite SL2(Z) as a central ±1 extension

ideas.what: Element of Γ_Q^~ as pair (α,β) satisfying the loop equation αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ℓ_1^ν
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (two- and three-cycle relations) in path/torsor form
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; this 'équation des lacets' manuscript is the source

ideas.what: Action on the oriented cartographic group (Z/2*Z/3)^: ρ↦ξρ, σ↦ησ
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on the cartographic group (dessins d'enfants)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, Galois action on dessins), in outline

ideas.what: Lift to SL(2,Z)^ compatible with conjugation by diag(χ,1) on SL(2,Ẑ), with sign ε_2(χ) (χ mod 4) on the order-4 generator (next page)
ideas.modern_name: GT action on profinite SL2(Z) / B_3 with cyclotomic sign correction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura–Schneps (GT acting on Γ_{1,1}); Nakamura on elliptic π1

missed.claim: Grothendieck had his own derivation, via the genus-0 'équation des lacets', of an explicit action of the GT-type group Γ_Q^~ on SL(2,Z)^ = π1^(M_{1,1}). It is obtained by lifting the cartographic action through the cartesian square with SL(2,Ẑ) and a sign ε_2(χ) depending on χ mod 4. This predates the published formulas of Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, though it is unclear whether it adds anything beyond them.
missed.quote: Ainsi on a une opération de Γ_Q^~ sur Sl(2,Z)^ que je voudrais expliciter, utilisant le diagramme cartésien
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority/attribution for the genus-1 level of GT actions. The fibre-product approach with the explicit χ mod 4 sign is a clean way to pass from PSL to SL that may not be stated in this form in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, explicit working-out of the genus-1 GT/Galois action via a fibre-product trick and a mod-4 sign. It is interesting for attribution. However, the result itself (GT acting on profinite SL2(Z)/B_3 with cyclotomic twists) is known in the later literature, so it is not genuinely new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Under (11), the subscript/annotation is likely a coset involving the loops ℓ_0, ℓ_∞ (e.g. '{ℓ_0,ℓ_∞}·Π̂_{0,3}' or similar), not 'Π{0,τ_∞}'. The superscript on Π̂_{0,3} may be '±1' rather than '≠1'. Uncertain.
'qui opère sur G_{0,3}^{+^} ≃ Sl(2,Z)^/±1' (the ±1 is cut off in the transcription).
The line 'M_{0,3}^~(0) ≃ Γ_Q^~' has a corrected subscript; the margin addition reads 'N_{1,1}^~(0) ≃ Γ_Q^~', which overwrites it in the sentence 'Ainsi on a une opération de Γ_Q^~ ...'.
